panels.title: OnimiaNet
notes: ROC panel for the model 'OnimiaNet' (model name printed in bold italics over the plot; it is a PDF text object centred at crop px (92, 53), inside this panel's image). Three step curves, one per EF class, and a dotted chance diagonal; x axis '1 - Specificity', y axis 'Sensitivity', tick labels 0.0-1.0 every 0.2 on both; the frame extends slightly past 0 and 1.

Rows are the AUROC of each curve as printed in the panel's legend: category = the EF class label exactly as printed (first line of the legend entry), value = the printed percentage, label_printed = the number as printed inside '(AUROC: xx.xx%)'. Legend order top to bottom: EF<40% (AUROC: 87.97%), salmon pink line; 40%≤EF<50% (AUROC: 65.74%), dark blue line; EF≥50% (AUROC: 76.77%), teal line.

Read from the PDF's embedded bitmap of this panel (a 900 x 900 px RGB image, 11.4 px per PDF point, about 7.6 x the bundle crop), where the legend digits are about 30 px tall; the same 15 strings also appear among Docling's OCR texts of page 6.
The curves themselves are not traced: see 'uncertain'.

uncertain: Convention: one row per ROC curve = its printed AUROC; category = EF class label, a single series 'AUROC' (the quantity printed in the legend), panel title = model name. Because the truth has one series per panel, the scorer ignores series names whenever the prediction also uses at most one series name per panel, and pairs rows by category. A prediction that puts the EF class in 'series' instead (three series per panel) with category/x null, or that returns points traced along the curves, does not pair with these rows; that is a difference of convention, not a reading error.

kind is 'line' (ROC curves), the natural kind. The recorded values are AUROC percentages (56-98), not positions on the 0-1 Sensitivity axis, so axes.y.range is deliberately null: with a 0-1 range the scorer (verify.axis_span -> y axis for a vertical 'line') would normalise an AUROC error by 1.0 instead of by the values' own span. With range null it falls back to the span of the panel's values, 0..max AUROC (88-98), so a prediction within about 1.8 AUROC points scores as a hit at 0.02. The y tick labels (0.0-1.0) are still listed in axes.y.ticks. No other kind changes this: 'other' has the same value axis.

The step curves were not traced point by point: the schema has one 'value' per row and the scorer pairs rows by exact x, while an ROC curve is a staircase of some 40-60 vertices at unlabelled x positions; mixing sensitivities (0-1) with AUROC percentages in one panel would also break the scorer's single value-axis normalisation. Tracing is possible from the 900 px bitmaps if a curve-shaped metric is ever added.
Values are in percent as printed (87.97, not 0.8797); label_printed is '87.97%' (the number with its unit; the full printed string is '(AUROC: 87.97%)').

Panel title 'OnimiaNet' is recorded as printed (probably a typo for 'OmniaNet'/'Omni...'; not corrected). Category '40%≤EF<50%' uses U+2264 and 'EF≥50%' U+2265, as the glyphs show; an ASCII prediction ('40%<=EF<50%', 'EF>=50%') is within the scorer's 0.2 edit distance for the first (2 of 12 = 0.17) but not for the second (2 of 7 = 0.29).

Panels are numbered 1-5 in reading order (OnimiaNet, H2former top row; EchoAgent right, vertically centred; MemSAM, EchoONE bottom row). bbox_px is each panel's embedded image clamped to the crop; neighbouring images overlap by about 2 px. figure.bbox is copied verbatim from the picture's prov in document.json (l, t, r, b with coord_origin BOTTOMLEFT, as in the existing truth files); bbox_px is in pixels of the bundle crop.
